content.thinking: I'm considering adding a dependabot ignore rule for the broken oxfmt 0.80.0 version so it skips to the next release, while noting the reviewer should still verify 0.81.0 actually fixes the issue before merging. I'll also add a comment explaining why and log this in the changelog's Unreleased/Fixed section.

// @pit: {"label": "Add dependabot ignores for broken oxc releases and changelog entry"}
async ({ workspace: { edit } }) => Promise.all([
  edit(".github/dependabot.yml", { revision: "TZXW5idEIziP", changes: [{ kind: "insertAfter", anchor: "11:fgVL6", content:
`      # oxfmt 0.80.0 and oxlint 1.95.0 ship linux-x64 bindings that crash with SIGILL on
      # CPUs without BMI2 (oxc-project/oxc#30164, cv/pit#420). Before accepting a newer
      # release, check its linux-x64 .node binding for rorx/shlx/shrx/andn/bzhi with objdump.
      - dependency-name: oxfmt
        versions: ["0.80.0"]
      - dependency-name: oxlint
        versions: ["1.95.0"]` }] }),
  edit("CHANGELOG.md", { revision: "vwB2vxSDPQVI", changes: [{ kind: "insertAfter", anchor: "5:HaQuG", content:
`
### Fixed

- Pit pins Oxfmt 0.79.0 (from 0.80.0) and Oxlint 1.94.0 (from 1.95.0). The 0.80.0 and 1.95.0 linux-x64 bindings were built with BMI2 instructions and crash with \`Illegal instruction\` (SIGILL) on x86-64 CPUs without BMI2/AVX2, such as Ivy Bridge and older (oxc-project/oxc#30164, #420). Pit loads Oxfmt when its extension starts, so on those CPUs Pi crashed at startup.` }] }),
])
